HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 78-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.75, creatinine 0.81-0.82, hemoglobin 10.9-12.5, platelets 207-216, sodium 140, wbc 7-7.5; vitals dbp 64-69, heart_rate 68-74, map 84-87, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 119-125, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.77-0.82, hemoglobin 9.7-10.8, platelets 205-214, sodium 140, wbc 7-7.7; vitals dbp 65-70, heart_rate 70-74, map 83-86, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 119-125, spo2 97-98, temp 36.7-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 78-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
